entities.name: Hammurabi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Hammurabi, also spelled Hammurapi, was the sixth Amorite king of the Old Babylonian Empire, reigning from c. 1792 to c. 1750 BC. He was preceded by his father, Sin-Muballit, who abdicated due to failing health. During his reign, he conquered the city-states of Larsa, Eshnunna, and Mari. He ousted Ishme-Dagan I, the king of Assyria, and forced his son Mut-Ashkur to pay tribute, bringing almost all of Mesopotamia under Babylonian rule.

entities.name: Hammurabi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: King of Babylon (c. 1810–1750 BCE) who united Mesopotamia and promulgated the Code of Hammurabi — one of the earliest and most complete written legal codes, establishing principles of justice that influenced all subsequent legal traditions.
